Hi Anna —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion, I put together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) pull that focuses on the evaluation plan and the cost sanity checks you requested. Before we lock dates, I want to confirm a couple of cost assumptions so the PO/Procurement team has accurate numbers.

Quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm target QPS for the POC (estimated concurrent users/hits per minute)?
- Expected average prompt length (tokens in + tokens out) for the three sample flows you gave us?
- Any mandatory region constraints (we discussed us-east vs europe earlier)?

Near-term MAP items we propose (high level):
1) Week 0: finalize eval prompts & test dataset (we’ll provide a spreadsheet)
2) Week 1: deploy POC environment, baseline latency tests
3) Week 2: run 48-hour traffic simulation with KV-prefix caching and batching enabled
4) Week 3: collect token consumption and unit cost report + adjustment meeting

On cost modeling: our default assumptions for the simulation will be: 8k context, 1.5x output multiplier, batching window 30ms with target batch size ~12 for CPU/GPU mix, and KV caching enabled for stable session prefixes (expected cache hit 25–40%). We’ll output a tokens-per-dollar and estimated monthly run-rate you can plug into forecasts.

I’ve looped in Lauren for procurement cadence and Marissa for the unit-econ table — Marissa will attach the working spreadsheet with detailed numbers.

If these assumptions look off, tell us what to change and we’ll update the MAP. Once confirmed we’ll send a concise MAP PDF for signatures.

Best,

Hi team —

Attached is the unit_econ_breakdown.xlsx with three scenarios: conservative, expected, and optimistic. Notes below summarize the assumptions that feed the MAP conservative vs optimistic columns.

Key assumptions (spreadsheet tab "Assumptions" — summarized):
- Request profile: 250 RPM peak (4.17 rps) with 30% diurnal variability. Simulation window will ramp to 6 rps for short bursts.
- Token per req: conservative 180, expected 200, optimistic 120 (tokens in + out).
- Batching: we model a 30 ms batching window on our serving runtime. At 4–6 rps this yields median batch sizes 8–14 depending on concurrency. Conservatively we assume batch size = 8 for cost calc; expected = 12; optimistic = 16.
- KV / prefix caching: we included two scoping options:
  * Scoped flows only (two canonical prompts): cache hit 40% expected, 55% optimistic
  * Full-flow variety: cache hit 10% conservative, 20% expected
- Model variants: primary run uses quantized LLM-v2 (lower-cost variant); fallback to LLM-v2-pt (full precision) for tail cases; model mix assumed 90% quantized, 10% full.
- Runtime overhead and fixed infra: we amortize warm pools and control-plane costs into a fixed monthly surcharge (line item in sheet).

Sample outputs from spreadsheet (monthlyized at 30 days):
- Conservative: 250 RPM baseline => ~8.1M tokens/day => ~243M tokens/month; tokens/$ = 8500 tokens per dollar => est monthly run-rate $28.5k + $2.5k infra = $31k
- Expected: tokens/$ = 12,000 => est monthly $20.25k + $2.5k infra = $22.75k
- Optimistic (high batching & cache): tokens/$ = 17,000 => est monthly $14.3k + $2.5k infra = $16.8k

Caveats and risk items:
- If live traffic has more variability than the scoped flows, cache hit drops and tokens per dollar worsen quickly. MAP should include a quick eval metric early: "prefix-stability" score after 24 hours of traffic.
- Batching is workload-sensitive: for very low latency sub-second interactive flows we may need to tighten the batching window which increases costs. We show trade-offs in the sheet.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Ben: confirm that the MAP pdf includes both conservative & expected scenarios for procurement.
2) Anna: confirm which two flows you want scoped for the high-cache scenario. If you can share a short sample (5–10 representative prompts) we’ll seed the cache for the simulation.
3) Lauren: please advise on any PO / payment milestones we should reflect.

I attached unit_econ_breakdown.xlsx and a quick MAP draft (map_timeline_v1.pdf).
